_comment: Profiles added after baseline 2.9 (plans/voice-quality.md stage 5). Read by tools/voice-gate after profiles.json.
Not in the baseline: profiles.json and its inputs fingerprint do not change, so baseline-2.9 stays valid. This file has its own fingerprint (results.json added_inputs_fingerprint).
The corpus, receiver and analysis settings come from profiles.json.
compare_no_adapt: the profile also runs as <name>-no-adapt, without the send-leg feedback, for the gates with min_ref.

extra_seeds (stage 3b): the profile, and its no-adapt twin, also run with each extra seed as <name>@<seed>. The gate on bottleneck_delay_mean_ms_median reads the median over the seed and the extra seeds: which packets the tail-drop queue drops, and so NetEQ's target, depends on the jitter draws.

profiles.name: congestion
profiles.description: Congestion from the sender's own rate: 20 ms, 2 ms jitter, and from 10 s to 30 s a 56 kbps bottleneck with a 300 ms tail-drop queue (38 bytes of SRTP tag, UDP and IPv4 headers per packet). 64 kbps Opus is about 84 kbps on that link, 32 kbps about 52. Then the link is free again.

gates.note: stage 5 gate: the send bitrate steps down within 2 s after the network first loses more than 10 % of 2 s of packets
stage 5 gate, median over seeds 909, 910, 911 since stage 3b: the ladder drains the queue (mean delay in the bottleneck window at least 100 ms lower than without it)

stage 5 gate: the ladder costs at most 0.2 MOS. In-band FEC repairs the isolated tail-drop losses of a single flow, so without the ladder the bottleneck costs only delay, which PESQ does not score; the ladder trades at most 0.2 MOS of NetEQ time stretch (the queue drains) for the delay gain gated above
